hints: Combine the logarithms so that each side is written as a single logarithm.
Use the power law on $4\ln x$, then use the quotient law with $\ln 4$.
Equate the logarithm arguments and rearrange the resulting equation as an equation in $x^4$.
Take the admissible real root, check both logarithm arguments are positive, and round only at the end.
walkthrough:
Apply the power and quotient laws of logarithms to the right-hand side of $\ln(x^4 - 4) = 4\ln x - \ln 4$:
$$4\ln x = \ln(x^4)$$
$$4\ln x - \ln 4 = \ln(x^4) - \ln 4 = \ln\left(\dfrac{x^4}{4}\right)$$

Equate the arguments of the natural logarithms on both sides:
$$\ln(x^4 - 4) = \ln\left(\dfrac{x^4}{4}\right)$$
$$x^4 - 4 = \dfrac{x^4}{4}$$

Multiply both sides by 4 to clear fractions and collect terms in $x^4$:
$$4(x^4 - 4) = x^4$$
$$4x^4 - 16 = x^4$$
$$4x^4 - x^4 = 16$$
$$3x^4 = 16$$
$$x^4 = \dfrac{16}{3}$$

Take the fourth root, noting that $\ln x$ requires $x > 0$ and $\ln(x^4 - 4)$ requires $x^4 > 4$ (which holds since $\dfrac{16}{3} \approx 5.333 > 4$):
$$x = \left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}} = \dfrac{2}{3^{1/4}}$$

Evaluate numerically to 2 decimal places:
$$3^{1/4} \approx 1.316074$$
$$x = \dfrac{2}{1.316074} \approx 1.51967$$
Rounding to 2 decimal places gives $x = 1.52$ (the negative root is rejected because $\ln x$ is defined only for $x > 0$).

ai_rubric.Solving Exponential and Logarithmic Equa: Logarithm laws give $4(x^4-4)=x^4$; solving subject to the logarithm domain gives $x=1.52$.
